newsitem.title: GERMANY: East Germany seen taking decades to close gap.
newsitem.headline: East Germany seen taking decades to close gap.

text.p: Closing the economic gap between formerly communist east Germany and the west will take at least 15 to 20 years, the Federation of German Industry (BDI) said.

As economic growth in the east slows to about three percent this year from six percent last year and eight percent in 1994, people in both regions should be more patient and lower their expectations, BDI said in a special report.
"Economic policymakers, employers and unions must accept this reality and heed it in a responsible way," BDI said.

Eastern wages in some sectors are approaching western levels, but gross domestic product (GDP) per capita in the east is still only 53 percent of the western level, and industrial output per capita is one-third, BDI said.
High unit-labour costs and low productivity are leaving many eastern companies in the red, but profits are needed to finance new investment.
Total production in the east is 200 billion marks less than consumption -- a sum equivalent to 40 percent of eastern GDP, and five percent of western GDP.
This difference must be financed by transfers from the west, contributing to the high burden of taxes and other withholdings from income, and to Germany's large public-sector indebtedness, BDI said.

It said that German and European Union aid for investments in the east and efforts to even out wages in the two regions should continue, but said that most workers consider job security more important that steady rises in compensation.
"Enterprises in western Germany want to do their part to build up the east," the report said. "But they can only do as much as their business situation allows."
